dossier.public_summary: This 12.3-day dip around an M dwarf looks planet-sized and flat-bottomed with one neighbour within one TESS pixel that could mimic it, but its depth halves in one sector and its three transits disagree, and difference images cannot place it on the target. The changing depth and lack of a stable on-target signal favour a blend or false alarm over a planet.

reasons.why: Depth varies significantly between sectors (3449, 3047, 1579 ppm) and p_constant below 0.01 points to a non-astrophysical or blended dip, not a stable planet transit.
Variation is within the same source (TESS-SPOC), so it reflects intrinsic change of the signal, not a calibration offset between products.

Only 3 transits and their depths are inconsistent (share 0.4805 of signal in few events), consistent with a few bad/transient dips rather than a repeating planet, with neighbours plausible_within_1px 1 that could cause the 2665 ppm dip with ~6-8% eclipses.

On-target confirmation is unavailable, and xgboost planet_rank 0.11 is low, so flat-bottom shape (v_sigma -3.889) and lack of secondary/odd_even cannot alone outweigh positive blend/variability evidence.
reasons.value: verdict inconclusive why no sector with a clear difference image

reasons.why: Duration ratio 1.323 is plausible for the M-dwarf, but size agreement does not establish planetary origin when depth is unstable.
